title: Congress Just Passed A Ban On “Intoxicating Hemp Products” So Complicated That Even Lawyers Aren’t Sure What It Means But We May Have A Year To Fix It

content_html_sanitized:
“No man's life, liberty, or property are safe while the Legislature is in session.” Judge Gideon John Tucker

 

Indeed, yesterday was not democracy’s finest hour. Even on Veterans Day, they still could not muster the basic decency to

vote to allow the Veterans Administration doctors even to recommend cannabis to veterans, something favored by an overwhelming majority of Americans.

See

Veterans Day And Medical Cannabis. Literally Adding Insult To Injury

 

And then, after being in recess for more than 50 days, they voted to return with a bill that included a ban on “intoxicating hemp”.

From Cato, the libertarian think tank

See

Congress Reopens the Government—and Reignites Prohibition

 

The best explanation of what happened that I have seen came from a Georgia law firm. The law does not go into effect for a year, so the industry and the public have time to mount a campaign to repeal it.

See SENATE PASSES BILL BANNING INTOXICATING HEMP PRODUCTS

 

As they noted, “One potential challenge to the new bill, for example, could be brought against any efforts by the government to ban hemp-derived Delta-8-THC as “synthesized or manufactured outside the plant.” Most chemical processes involving the manufacturing of Delta-8-THC are “semi-synthetic,” not synthetic, and Delta-8-THC can be extracted from hemp. Accordingly, certain Delta-8 products may not fall under this ban.

Additionally, the government’s attempt to prohibit products containing THC, THCA, and “any other cannabinoids that have similar effects,” as determined by HHS, can be attacked based on the unconstitutionally vague language that fails to provide lawful hemp businesses with sufficient notice of what cannabinoids are or are not allowed. There is also an argument that this language is unlawful under the “non-delegation” doctrine, under which congress can not delegate major questions to agencies like HHS.”

 

Kentucky Senator Rand Paul tried to protect his farm community, pointing out that this bill will hurt farmers nationally. Unfortunately, he was not successful.

 

In addition to farmers, there are a number of politically powerful groups that will join in the fight, including convenience stores.

See

A Seed of Opportunity

Intoxicating hemp beverages could represent a huge market for convenience—if it’s not locked out.

 

Convenience stores are also an important part of the ecosystem for people who make less than members of Congress.

 

Of course, most convenience stores also sell “intoxicating alcohol beverages”, to coin a phrase. Shhh! That is controlled by state law. The alcohol industry seems divided. Some see cannabis as a threat to their interests, but others have the good sense and basic principles to recognize the dangers of using the government to “prohibit” intoxicating beverages. Sound familiar??

 

The ultimate absurdity yesterday came from Rand Paul’s fellow Kentucky Senator, Mitch McConnell, who supported the original bill that legalized hemp, but now wants to repeal it…to protect the children, of course.

See

Kentucky GOP Sens. Rand Paul and Mitch McConnell are clashing over a provision that opponents say will destroy the growing hemp industry in America.

 

Sure thing, Senator!

Let’s look at how well Congress protects American children.

From US News: “U.S. Kids More Likely to Die Than Kids in 19 Other Nations. The U.S. could have spared 600,000 lives if it kept pace with other wealthy nations, a study finds.”

 

The U.S. has 5.1 deaths per live births. Canada has 4.3 deaths per live births. The Netherlands has 3.6. ((Cannabis has been sold over the counter there fifty years. )

 

From The World Economic Forum:

These are the countries where children are most satisfied with their lives.

Overall ranking

The Netherlands is ranked 1st.

The United States is ranked 36th, but we did beat Bulgaria!

 

See

This is why Dutch teenagers are among the happiest in the world

 

Think of the children, but don’t forget about the Veterans!
